This Minor Flood Warning is being issued for parts of the Goulburn River downstream of Shepparton. 

Minor flooding is possible on the Goulburn River at McCoys bridge overnight Saturday (15th August 2026) into Sunday. 

The Goulburn River at McCoys Bridge is currently at 8.17 metres and steady, below the minor flood level. 

The Goulburn River at McCoys Bridge may reach around the minor flood level (9.00 metres) overnight Saturday into Sunday.

This Advice replaces the Advice issued at 12:01pm Friday 14th of August 2026. 
Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and remain alert.
What you should do: 
  • People living or camping on the Goulburn River between Shepparton and Kanyapella should expect river level rises on Saturday as floodwater arrives from Shepparton. 
  • Farmers should consider moving livestock and machinery from along the river to higher ground. 
  • Be prepared to act if your situation changes.
  • Monitor river levels. Go to www.bom.gov.au/vic/warnings/
  • Stay informed by listening to emergency broadcasters and monitoring warnings.
Impacts in your area: 
  • High river levels and potential flooding in areas close to rivers and streams.
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

The next update is expected by 16/08/2026 12:00 pm or as the situation changes.

properties.location: the Murray River from Yarrawonga to Barmah
properties.webBody:
This Flood Advice is being issued for the Murray River from Yarrawonga to Barmah.

Water releases from Yarrawonga Weir are expected to cause river level rises along the Murray River between Yarrawonga and Barmah over the coming days

River levels are expected to rise gradually and may inundate low lying areas adjacent to the river.  Conditions may change over the coming days as river levels respond to the water releases.

Rises are forecast to remain below the minor flood level.

Campsites, sections of parkland, and areas close to the riverbank are likely to be affected. Campers are encouraged to move to higher ground or safer locations.

Floodwater may impact access tracks, making them impassable to all vehicle types. 

Access to some campsites and recreational areas may become restricted.
Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and remain alert.
What you should do
  • You are responsible for your own safety and the safety of those in your care.
  • If you are camping or staying near the Murray River, monitor river conditions and be prepared to relocate to higher ground if required.
  • Move vehicles, caravans, camping equipment and other belongings away from low-lying areas before access is cut off.
  • Parks Victoria has closed some park access gates due to the rising river levels. These closures are in place for your safety. Do not bypass closed gates or attempt to access closed areas via private farm gates or other alternative routes.
  • Do not drive through floodwater or around road closure signs.Avoid walking through flooded areas.
  • Stay informed by monitoring warnings and following the advice of emergency services and land managers.
Impacts in your area
  • High river levels and potential flooding in areas close to rivers and streams. 
  • Parks, hiking tracks and campgrounds may be closed due to flooding. To find out more go to https://www.parks.vic.gov.au/coc-listing?region=Northeast+Victoria
  • Caravan parks and camping grounds may be flooded. 
  • Areas around rivers and streams may be flooded. 
  • Boating in floodwaters is dangerous due to debris, submerged trees and other hidden dangers. 
This message was issued by State Emergency Service 

The next update is expected by 17/08/2026 12:00 pm or as the situation changes.

Use multiple sources to stay informed:
  • www.emergency.vic.gov.au 
  • VicEmergency Hotline - freecall 1800 226 226
  • VicEmergency app 
  • Facebook
  • Tune in to ABC Local Radio, commercial and designated community radio stations, or News24 TV.
Accessibility:
The following services can help you, or someone you know, access information during an emergency.
  • To access this information in other languages, call the Translating and Interpreting Service on 131 450 (freecall) and ask them to call VicEmergency Hotline.   
  • If you are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech/communication impairment, contact the National Relay Service and ask them to call the VicEmergency Hotline.

properties.webBody:
This Minor Flood Warning is being issued for the Goulburn River, Seymour to Shepparton including Mooroopna and Kialla.

The Goulburn River at Shepparton is currently at 9.89 metres and steady, with minor flooding. The Goulburn River at Shepparton is likely to remain above the minor flood level (9.50 metres) for the remainder of Saturday and into Sunday.

The Broken River at Orrvale and Seven Creeks at Kialla West are now both below minor flood level. 

This Advice replaces the Advice issued at 11:54am Friday the 14th of August 2026. 
Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and remain alert.
What you should do: 
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never drive, walk or ride through floodwater.
  • Farmers should consider moving livestock and machinery to higher ground.
  • Be prepared to act if your situation changes.
  • Contact family members and neighbours to ensure they are aware of the situation.
  • Stay informed by listening to emergency broadcasters and monitoring warnings.
To check if your property is prone to flooding, 
  • Check the Goulburn Broken Catchment Management Authority's Community Flood Information Portal and download your property information statement at: https://my.floodreport.com.au/gbcma/
  • For full instructions, and more local flood information, download the Shepparton, Mooroopna & Kialla Local Flood Guide at: www.ses.vic.gov.au/plan-and-stay-safe/flood-guides/greater-shepparton-city-council
  • Try the new Greater Shepparton Emergency Dashboard https://emergency.greatershepparton.com.au/ to view local emergency information.
Impacts in the Shepparton, Mooroopna and Kialla areas:
  • The Ross Edwards Causeway is not expected to close.
  • Riverside areas and flats will be flooded for several days, including camps, areas near the Shepparton Lawn tennis court and Princess Park near the Bocce club and behind Aquamoves.  
  • High river levels and potential flooding of farmland and parks close to the rivers and creeks.
  • Watt Road closed both directions between Riverview Drive and McLennan Street. 
  • Riverview Drive closed both directions between Botanic Gardens Avenue and Watt Road.
  • Raftery Road closed both directions between Edgewater Road, Kialla and Seven Creeks Drive.
  • All vehicle & walking tracks within the Arcadia Streamside Reserve, Shepparton Regional Park & Gemmills Swamp Wildlife Reserve were closed on Monday. 
  • Floodwater may cover South Quinnan Parade and Hassett Street near Lincoln Drive.
  • In Shepparton, Stewart Reserve, the fenced dog park, Jaycee Park and the Swans Football/Netball club may be impacted by floodwater. 
  • There is floodwater in Jordan Place, Shepparton near The Boulevard. 
Impacts at Toolamba:
  • Tracks in the forested areas west of Goulburn River, such as Steves Track will be flooded.
Road Closures
  • Other local roads may be closed and low bridges may be underwater.
  • For the latest road closures go to: traffic.transport.vic.gov.au
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

The next update is expected by 16/08/2026 12:00 pm or as the situation changes.

The King River at Docker Road is estimated to be around the minor flood level and falling slowly. The King River at Docker Road Bridge may remain around the minor flood level (3.70 metres) during Saturday. 

This Advice message replaces the Advice issued at 11:37am Friday the 14th August 2026.  

Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and remain alert.

This Minor Flood Warning is being issued for Avon-Richardson Rivers.

Minor flooding is easing along the Richardson River at Donald Town.

The Richardson River at Donald Town is currently at 2.37 metres and steady, with minor flooding. The main flood peak passed Donald Town late Friday (14th August 2026) evening.

The Richardson River at Donald Town is likely to remain above the minor flood level (2.20 metres) overnight Saturday into Sunday.

This is an update, replacing the Advice message issued at 2:10pm Friday 14th August 2026 .
Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and remain alert.
What you should do: 
  • Be prepared to act if your situation changes.
  • Stay informed by listening to emergency broadcasters and monitoring warnings.
  • Farmers should still consider moving livestock and machinery to higher ground.
  • Contact family members and neighbours to ensure they are aware of the situation.
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never drive, walk or ride through floodwater.
  • Monitor weather forecasts and river levels. Go to www.bom.gov.au/vic/warnings
Impacts in your area: 
  • Flood barriers are in place at camp street Donald and being monitored by council.
  • High river levels and potential flooding in areas close to rivers and streams.
  • Local roads may be closed and low bridges may be underwater.
  • Boating in floodwaters is dangerous due to debris, submerged trees and other hidden dangers. 
  • Stagnant water can be harmful to your health. Don’t swim, drink or wash in stagnant water.
  • Some roads may be closed or unsafe to travel on due to floodwater. 
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

The next update is expected by 1.30pm Saturday the 15th August 2026 or as the situation changes.

Use multiple sources to stay informed:
  • www.emergency.vic.gov.au
  • VicEmergency Hotline - freecall 1800 226 226
  • VicEmergency app
  • Facebook
  • Tune in to ABC Local Radio, commercial and designated community radio stations, or News24 TV.
  • For road closure information go to www.traffic.transport.vic.gov.au or phone 13 11 70.
  • For relief and recovery information go to www.emergency.vic.gov.au/relief.
Accessibility: 
The following services can help you, or someone you know, access information during an emergency. 
  • To access this information in other languages, call the Translating and Interpreting Service on 131 450 (freecall) and ask them to call VicEmergency Hotline. 
  • If you are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech/communication impairment, contact the National Relay Service and ask them to call the VicEmergency Hotline.
